record.paper_title: Developments, Applications and Open Problems in Fixed Point Theory
record.original_question: Let K be a bounded closed convex subset of a Banach space, and let T,G: K -> K be commuting nonexpansive mappings. For epsilon > 0, define the epsilon-approximate fixed point set of a map S by F_epsilon(S) = {x in K : ||x - Sx|| <= epsilon}. Must F_epsilon(T) intersect F_epsilon(G) nontrivially for every epsilon > 0?

evidence.quote: Another problem concerns approximate fixed point sequences. It's well-established that if K is a bounded convex subset of any Banach space (or normed space), and T: K -> K is nonexpansive, then there exists a sequence {x_n} in K such that ||x_n - T(x_n)|| tends to 0 as n approaches infinity. Consequently, for each epsilon > 0, F_epsilon(T) := {x in K : ||x - Tx|| <= epsilon} != empty.

Problem 2: If K is a bounded (closed) convex subset of a Banach space and if T,G: K -> K are commuting nonexpansive mappings, is it the case that for each epsilon > 0, F_epsilon(T) cap F_epsilon(G) != empty?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a Banach space and let $K \subset X$ be a bounded, closed, convex, nonempty subset. A mapping $S: K \to K$ is called nonexpansive if $\|Sx - Sy\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$. Two mappings $T, G: K \to K$ are said to commute if $T \circ G = G \circ T$. For a self-map $S: K \to K$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, define the $\varepsilon$-approximate fixed point set
$$F_\varepsilon(S) := \{x \in K : \|x - Sx\| \le \varepsilon\}.$$
It is known that for any nonexpansive $S: K \to K$, the set $F_\varepsilon(S)$ is nonempty for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

Question: Suppose $T, G : K \to K$ are commuting nonexpansive mappings. Is it necessarily true that
$$F_\varepsilon(T) \cap F_\varepsilon(G) \neq \emptyset \quad \text{for every } \varepsilon > 0?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether two commuting nonexpansive self-maps on a bounded closed convex subset of a Banach space share common approximate fixed points (for every $\varepsilon>0$) is a well-known open question in metric fixed point theory. While Bruck and others established existence of common fixed points under additional structure (e.g., weak compactness plus FPP/CFPP), no general resolution for arbitrary bounded closed convex subsets of Banach spaces appears in the literature. Recent surveys and articles continue to list it among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Normal Structure and Common Fixed Point Properties for Semigroups of Nonexpansive Mappings in Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Bruck proved common fixed point results under weak compactness plus FPP/CFPP assumptions; general Banach-space case for commuting pairs remains restricted.
status_evidence.claim: Common fixed point theorems for commuting nonexpansive maps require additional hypotheses beyond boundedness, suggesting the bare approximate-version remains open.

status_evidence.title: Fixed Point Problems for Nonexpansive Mappings in Bounded Sets of Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open questions about approximate fixed points and common fixed points for commuting nonexpansive mappings on bounded convex subsets.
status_evidence.claim: The question of common approximate fixed points for two commuting nonexpansive maps on a bounded closed convex subset of a Banach space is treated as an open problem.
